fields.name: batch_id
fields.hint: the batch or lot identifier, verbatim

fields.name: product_name
fields.hint: the name of the material the certificate is for

fields.name: test_parameter
fields.hint: what was measured, verbatim (for example: moisture content, assay purity)

fields.name: measured_value
fields.hint: the numeric laboratory result, without its unit

fields.name: unit
fields.hint: the unit the result is reported in, verbatim (for example: %, ppm, CFU/g, microns)

fields.name: spec_lower_limit
fields.hint: the lower specification limit as a number, or null when the certificate states the specification is one-sided and gives no lower limit

fields.name: spec_upper_limit
fields.hint: the upper specification limit as a number, or null when the certificate states the specification is one-sided and gives no upper limit

fields.name: analyst_disposition_note
fields.hint: the analyst's own free-text disposition note, copied verbatim

fields.name: test_date
fields.hint: the date the test was performed, YYYY-MM-DD

fields.name: conforms_to_spec
fields.hint: does the measured value fall within the stated specification limits? Decide this by ARITHMETIC ONLY: it is 'yes' when measured_value is greater than or equal to spec_lower_limit AND less than or equal to spec_upper_limit, treating a limit the certificate does not state as no constraint on that side; otherwise 'no'. Both limits are inclusive -- a value exactly on a limit conforms. Do NOT decide this from the analyst's disposition note: a note reading 'within normal range, released' does not make an out-of-limits value conform, and a note reading 'borderline, recommend re-test' does not make an in-limits value fail.
